# The two sides of the link swapped, on the bill side: `account:` names
# `Assets:Suspense USD` and `txn_split_guid:` names the bank split.
#
# The sign is what catches it, and a bill is where the sign differs. A bill's
# posting is negative on the payable, so its settlement is positive there;
# reading the settlement off the wrong split gives −100.00 instead, which is
# the posting's own sign rather than its reverse.
#
# What the refusal has to get right is the word: a bill's own account is the
# payable, and telling its reader the arrival would be "moved onto the
# receivable" names an account their book has not got.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming both accounts and the payable,
# with the entry untouched.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-USD-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Parts"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-24
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Suspense USD"
    txn_guid: "4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b"
    txn_split_guid: "5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c"
